scope: Biopharmaceutics and pharmacokinetics for third-year pharmacy students: equation correctness, unit consistency, model assumptions, and whether every worked calculation can be reproduced from the printed steps.
criteria: Every equation is dimensionally consistent and its symbols are defined where first used.
Units are carried through each calculation step and the final answer carries the right unit.
Ln and log10 forms are not mixed; the 2.303 factor appears only where the base changes.
Model assumptions are stated before the equations they justify (one- versus two-compartment, first- versus zero-order).
Elimination rate constant, half-life, volume of distribution and clearance are related consistently (CL = Ke x Vd).
Apparent volume of distribution is described as apparent, not as a physiological volume.
Absorption parameters are distinguished: Ka and tmax describe rate, AUC and F describe extent.
Superposition, steady state and accumulation are derived, not asserted.
Non-linear kinetics uses Michaelis-Menten terms correctly (Vmax, Km) and says when linear equations stop applying.
Bioequivalence acceptance criteria, BCS classes and dissolution apparatus are stated as the current regulatory texts state them.
Every worked example is reproducible: each arithmetic step is shown and the printed answer is recomputed.
Graph descriptions match the plot: semilog axes, slope sign and intercept meaning.
exclusions: Do not request topics outside the source syllabus; this rework simplifies and organises, it does not broaden.
Do not request clinical dosing recommendations for named patients.
evidence_expectations: Quote the exact text and give file and line for every finding.
Recompute any number challenged, and show the recomputation.
Give replacement text, not only a critique.
Cite a standard text or the regulatory document for any corrected definition or criterion.
